Sticks, blocks and pounds

American butter comes in 1-pound boxes of four sticks, and every stick is the same: 4 ounces, 113 grams, ½ cup or 8 tablespoons. The wrapper is marked in tablespoons, so cutting along the lines is as accurate as a scale. East Coast sticks are long and thin and West Coast sticks are short and stubby, but they weigh exactly the same.

Most of the rest of the world sells butter in 250 g blocks, which is about 2¼ US sticks. When a European or Australian recipe says "1 block of butter", that's 250 g: two sticks plus about 2 tablespoons. Melted butter weighs the same as solid, so a recipe that calls for melted butter by the cup still means 113 g per half cup.

For butter's other conversions, like ⅛ cup or 3 cups, see the butter cups to grams chart.

Questions

How many grams is a stick of butter?

One US stick of butter is 113 g, which is 4 ounces, ½ cup or 8 tablespoons.

How many sticks of butter are in a cup?

Two. One cup of butter is 2 sticks, 16 tablespoons or 227 g.

How many sticks is 250 g of butter?

250 g is about 2¼ sticks: 2 sticks plus about 2 tablespoons. It’s the standard size of a European butter block.

Does melted butter measure the same as solid butter?

By weight, yes: 113 g is 113 g. By volume it’s close enough for most recipes, though solid butter packed into a cup can trap air. Weighing avoids the question.
